Prediction error can be resolved two ways: revise the model, or act on the
world until the sensory evidence matches it. One account treats delusion as a
pathology of the first route, though that remains an active debate rather than
a settled finding. Akathisia may be a pathology of the second — an inner
restlessness that may be the felt quality of an error no action can close.

Aripiprazole makes this testable. A D2 partial agonist does not simply lower
dopaminergic signalling; it compresses it toward an intermediate set point,
damping rather than removing its dependence on endogenous tone. If dopamine
encodes the precision of prediction errors, partial agonism acts as what I
will call a precision clamp — the term is mine, not the literature's — and the
prediction is a loss of context-dependent adjustment rather than a shifted
baseline.
